reuse.why: All four steps go through the tree's existing getBulkBudgetCategories selection and averageToBudget sign helper, plus the shared extractTagsFromText for the #fixed tag; the new action reuses the bulk selection, setBudget, batchMessages and the undoable/mutator registration.

duplication.why: No rule is copied across actions; only small local code (a JSON.parse length check for goal_def, a per-category sum-amount sheet read) resembles logic elsewhere (goal-template getTemplates, getCategoryAverage) without being a real copy.

placement.why: The exclusion rules live in the one selection function in budget/actions.ts, the new action sits with its siblings and is registered in budget/app.ts like the others.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests and tests, but includes an unrelated import reordering in server/schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: Which categories a month-wide action writes is decided in one documented function with one explicit flag, so later rules (#fixed, templates, hidden opt-in) were each a single edit.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth, setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg all take their categories from getBulkBudgetCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: None; hasSavedTemplates is a minimal check rather than a reshaped copy of getTemplates.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories keeps two parameters (includeHidden renamed to includeHiddenCategories, skipMissingGroup unchanged); the #fixed and saved-template checks are uniform rule clauses applied to every caller, not per-caller special cases; no call site filters categories on its own.
